kind: account addendum after measurement, before the change is committed
finding: BF cr_yaml_u_escape now renders (exit 0, no export error) but does not match: Java's text is 'Vault \U0010FFFD end' (textLength 154.4717), the escape kept literally. The account assumed Java decodes the YAML escape; it does not. cr_json_u_escape matches (Java's JSON parser decodes \uDBFF\uDFFD).
java_trace: yaml/parser/YamlLine.java#build (51-94): a line's key and value are split at the first colon outside quotes (findColonSeparator 98-113) and passed through unquote (189-198), which only removes one pair of surrounding quotes. No escape sequence of a key, a value, a '- ' item or a key-less line is decoded; a backslash and what follows it stay as written.
Flow sequences ('[...]', toList 115-180) are the exception: there a backslash makes the next character literal.
rust_cause: parse_yaml_diagram hands the body to serde_yml, whose double-quoted scalars decode YAML escapes (\U, \u, \n, \", \\ ...).
planned_change: Before serde_yml, a double-quoted key or value that Java's YamlLine.build would unquote (the whole key, the whole value, a '- ' item, or a key-less line, comments removed as removeYamlComment does) and that contains a backslash is handed to serde single-quoted with the same characters (a quote doubled per YAML single-quote rules), so serde returns them unchanged, as unquote does. Scalars without a backslash decode identically either way and are left alone; flow sequences are left to serde (declared residue).
declared_residue: Flow-sequence items keep serde's double-quoted decoding where Java makes the next character literal.
Single-quoted scalars keep YAML's '' -> ' (Java's unquote keeps both quotes); multi-line quoted scalars keep serde's folding. Neither involves a backslash.

precommitted_measurement.expect: outputs change only for @startyaml sources with a backslash inside a double-quoted key or value (no golden has one); zero lost matches
